name: At a glance: a read-out of the network with shortcuts to the people behind it
summary: Right after an upload, the first thing on the page is one written paragraph saying what the network is: who is in it, where they work, what they are tagged with and where they are based. Below it are up to six ranked shortcuts built from the file, such as "22 at Stripe", "107 tagged prospect" or "85 connected in the last 12 months". Pressing a shortcut lights exactly those people on the globe and lists them, without rebuilding the layout. These shortcuts replace the fixed Raise/Source/Diligence/Largest company bar, the lens gauges and the fixed example questions. Grouping defaults, group labels and example questions all come from the same profile of the file.
firstScreen:
Order after an upload. The page scrolls to the map section, not to the top.
1. A one-line source strip: "544 LinkedIn contacts · kept in your account · Manage". Manage opens the old Sources card.
2. The read-out card, headed "Your network at a glance".
VC sample: "You know 544 people at 254 companies: 109 investors and 108 engineers. The most at Stripe (22) and Google (19). Strongest in Software (66). 85 connected in the last 12 months."
Shortcuts: [109 investors] [108 engineers] [22 at Stripe] [19 at Google] [66 in Software] [85 connected in the last 12 months]
Ask line: "Ask your network", with chips "Who do I know at Stripe?", "Which investors do I know?", "Who do I know at Google?"
3. The globe on the left (about 60% wide). On the right is the people panel. Before any press it is headed "Everyone · 544", sorted most senior first, with the seniority bar and the Next layer bars.
4. Below the globe: the breadcrumb, the grouping switch and "Find a person or company".
Sales CRM sample: source strip "328 contacts from sales-crm.csv · kept in your account · Manage".
Read-out: "328 contacts at 147 companies. By tag: 107 prospect, 73 customer, 69 partner. Biggest account: Marlowe Department Stores (18), then Bayview Health System (16). Most are in New York (63)."
Shortcuts: [107 tagged "prospect"] [73 tagged "customer"] [69 tagged "partner"] [18 at Marlowe Department Stores] [16 at Bayview Health System] [63 in New York]
Ask chips: "Who do I know at Marlowe Department Stores?", "Who do I know in New York?", "Who do I know at Bayview Health System?"
The globe opens grouped By tag, with hubs prospect / customer / partner / decision maker / champion / churned. The panel reads "Everyone · 328".
Pressing "22 at Stripe" turns the chip to its active style with a close mark. All 22 Stripe people, across all three role branches, stay bright while everything else dims, and the camera turns to them. The panel heading becomes "22 at Stripe · Clear" and lists the 22.
networkProfile:
profileNetwork(contacts) is computed once per contact set, client side, with no model. N = number of contacts.
Fields count as present when filled share is at least: location 30%, tags 30%, connectedOn 50%, company 50%.
Roles use classifyContact with two fixes:
(a) Tags are never tested against role title patterns.
(b) If a role was hit by company only (investor, lp, clinician) and the title, classified on its own, gives a specific role, or contains an operator word (engineer, product, design, sales, marketing, manager, administrator, buyer, procurement, data, cto, vp, head) and no invest/portfolio/fund, then the title wins.
"Cardiologist|oncologist|radiologist|neurologist|pediatrician" are added to the clinician title vocabulary.
Families: investors = investor + lp; then one family per role (founders and CEOs, clinicians, researchers and academics, bankers, lawyers...). Operators, executives and professionals are split by title into engineers, product and design people, or sales and marketing people.
Kind, first rule that matches:
- fundraising: investors ≥ 60%
- pipeline: tags present and at least 2 tags each covering 5-80%
- investor: investors ≥ 15%
- clinical: clinicians + academics ≥ 30%
- operator: everything else
Small network: N < 30. The read-out then drops the industry and recency sentences.

presets.label: {n} tagged "{tag}"
presets.when: Tags are present (≥30% of rows) and the tag covers 5-80% of N with at least 3 people. Top 3 by count. Only these kinds rank them first: pipeline, fundraising.
presets.action: Sets activePreset = {id:'tag:'+tag, label, ids}. highlightIds becomes those people. The atlas is not rebuilt, so the globe dims everyone else and turns to the lit people. The panel heading becomes the label plus 'Clear', and it lists exactly those people, most senior first. Pressing it again, or pressing Clear, removes the highlight.
presets.why: In a CRM or LP list, the stage the user already tracks (prospect, committed, churned) is the question they come with.

presets.label: {n} {family plural}, e.g. "109 investors", "192 engineers", "79 clinicians"
presets.when: Family covers 5-90% of N with at least 3 people. Executive, operator and professional never appear unsplit. The top 2 show, or the top 1 for pipeline and fundraising. Investors are skipped for fundraising (they are everyone).
presets.action: Same as tag: lights every member of the family through highlightIds, and the panel lists them. If grouped by role and all members sit in one role hub, the camera flies to that hub with goTo.
presets.why: This replaces Raise/Source/Diligence with a count of real people that actually discriminates.

presets.label: {n} at {company}
presets.when: Companies counted with groupByCompany(contacts), whole network, excluding 'No company listed', each with at least 3 people and at least 2% of N. Top 2.
presets.action: Lights every contact whose normalizeCompanyKey matches, so all slices across branches light up. selectedId is set to that company's largest node, so its branch pulses. The panel lists all n, with a 'Company profile' link at the top. Replaces 'Largest company'.
presets.why: Gives the true largest employers (Stripe 22, not a Google slice of 12) and is visibly the company the chip names.

presets.label: {n} in {industry}
presets.when: Top industryOf label that is a sector, not a function fallback (excluded: Other, Founders & CEOs, Investing, Engineering & data, Product & design, Sales & marketing, Finance & operations, People & talent, Legal & policy, Research & teaching, Students, Self-employed), covering 10-80% of N. 'Venture capital' is skipped when the investors chip is shown.
presets.action: Lights the people with that industryOf label, filtered on the client and never sent through the question engine. The panel lists them.
presets.why: Says where the network is strongest, in words.

presets.label: {n} in {city}
presets.when: Location present (≥30%). The city is the first comma part of the location. The top city needs at least 8% of N.
presets.action: Lights the people whose city matches, and the panel lists them.
presets.why: Helps with trips and in-person meetings. Appears only when the file has locations.

presets.label: {n} connected in the last 12 months
presets.when: connectedOn present (≥50%) and at least 5 people have connectedOn within 365 days of today.
presets.action: Lights them. The panel lists them newest first.
presets.why: Fresh relationships are the warmest ones to ask. LinkedIn files carry this date and today nothing uses it.

presets.label: {n} decision makers
presets.when: seniority()==0 covers 10-60% of N, and there is no tag literally named 'decision maker'. It only fills a free slot.
presets.action: Lights them. The panel lists them.
presets.why: Answers who can actually say yes.

labelsAndGroupings:
Shortcut order depends on the kind:
- pipeline and fundraising: tag(3), company(2), place(1), role(1), industry, senior, recent
- all others: role(2), company(2), industry(1), place(1), recent(1), senior(1)
At most 6 show. When the slots fill, the remaining candidates are dropped.
The read-out sentences are templates fed from the same chips:
- "You know {N} people at {C} companies: {role1} and {role2}."
- "The most at {co1} ({n}) and {co2} ({n})."
- "Strongest in {industry} ({n})."
- "{recent} connected in the last 12 months."
For pipeline: "{N} contacts at {C} companies. By tag: {t1 n} {t1}, {t2 n} {t2}, {t3 n} {t3}. Biggest account: {co1} ({n}), then {co2} ({n}). Most are in {city} ({n})."
For fundraising: "{N} contacts at {C} organisations, {inv} of them investors or allocators. By tag: …".
A sentence whose rule fails is left out, never padded.
Every bold number in the read-out is a button that does the same thing as its chip.
Grouping switch:
- Add a 'By tag' grouping (each contact's first tag, MAX_HUBS cap). It is the default for pipeline and fundraising.
- The default is role for every other kind.
- Country is hidden, not disabled, when location is under 30%.
- By company caps the top-level clusters at 16, with the rest folded into "Other companies". This is required: the current version freezes for 31.6 s on the VC sample.
- A one-bucket root layer is skipped, so the LP list stops showing a single "Investors & LPs 114".
- Role hub hints become neutral ("From job titles"). The fund-manager phrasing goes.
layout:
Top to bottom:
1. Source strip, one line (Manage expands the full Sources card and Remove all).
2. Read-out card: paragraph, shortcut row, and the ask input with 3 example chips. The answer renders inside this card, directly under the input, and lights people the same way a shortcut does.
3. A two-column map section: globe (60%) and people panel (40%), stacked on phones.
4. Breadcrumb, grouping switch and find box in one toolbar under the globe.
Removed:
- the preset bar (Whole network, Raise capital, Source deals, Diligence, Largest company)
- the dashboard lens gauges and panelLens
- the Layers steps (the breadcrumb is the only location indicator)
- the Zoom-to bar (the panel's Next layer bars do this)
- the back chip
- dead companyFilter state
- the setExpanded call in Remove all
Merged: Whole network, All and Fit become Fit plus the active chip's Clear.
Kept: the globe, find box, Filter these people, details panel, Founder check, intro paths, the direct-only toggle and source chips.
Lens words stay understood in typed questions, but no button shows them.
Tokens only: readableOn and the fallback colours move to tokens, and the arbitrary text sizes go.
Globe change: when lit people span more than 1.1 rad, zoom out to home and pulse the lit dots once, so a press is always visible.

questions:
Example questions are built only in forms the rule engine already parses, and only from values that exist in the file:
1. "Who do I know at {co1}?"
2. a role question when a role chip exists ("Which investors do I know?", "Which clinicians do I know?"), using the 17 regex role groups
3. "Who do I know in {city}?" when there is a place chip; otherwise "Who do I know at {co2}?"
"Intro paths to {co}" is offered only after a company chip is pressed, as a link in the panel.
Tag, industry and recency are never phrased as questions until the engine gains tag, industry and date filters. Their chips filter on the client.
The rotating placeholder uses the same three questions. EXAMPLES at network.js L56 is deleted.
acceptance: profileNetwork on vc-investor-linkedin.csv returns kind 'investor' and chips exactly ['109 investors','108 engineers','22 at Stripe','19 at Google','66 in Software','85 connected in the last 12 months'] with today fixed at 2026-11-21
profileNetwork on sales-crm.csv returns kind 'pipeline', first chip '107 tagged "prospect"', and the investors family count is 0 (tags are not tested against role titles)
founder-operator-linkedin.csv: the investors family is ≤ 5 (company-only investor hits with operator titles are reclassified)
lp-fundraising-list.csv: kind 'fundraising', no investors chip, default grouping 'tag'
healthcare-academic.csv: no chip and no read-out text mentions raise, source, diligence or investors
Pressing '22 at Stripe' on the VC sample sets highlightIds to exactly the 22 Stripe person ids across all role branches, does not call buildAtlas, and the panel heading reads '22 at Stripe'
Pressing an active chip again empties highlightIds and restores the panel to 'Everyone · N'
No chip, sentence or example question names a company, tag or city absent from the uploaded file (all 6 fixtures)
Example questions for sales-crm contain 'Marlowe Department Stores' and none contain Google or Stripe; each, sent to the query rules, returns total > 0
No chip renders with a count of 0 or a count equal to N, for every fixture
Country is not rendered in the grouping switch for the three LinkedIn fixtures
groupBy 'company' on vc-investor-linkedin.csv lays out in under 500 ms with at most 16 top clusters
Remove all deletes the data and shows no error notice
network.js contains no hex colour literals and no arbitrary text-[..px] classes
risks:
- The counts depend on the classifier fixes. Without them, the CRM shows "69 investors". Ship the fixes together with the read-out.
- A file's first tag stands for a contact that has several tags, so the By tag grouping is lossy. The chips count every tag.
- City parsing takes the first comma part, so "Greater Boston Area" and "Boston, MA" count as two cities. Normalise with the existing countryOf aliases.
- A highlight spread over the whole globe can still look subtle; this needs the zoom-out and pulse change.
- "Strongest in Healthcare (165)" says little on a hospital network. The 80% cap could drop to 60% after testing on real files.
- Dropping the lens buttons removes a VC-specific feature. Investors and founders chips cover it.
